items.name: Software Defined Networks (SDN)
items.description: SDNs can be used to virtually define a WAN or set of WAN network topology. This means that the IP Addresses and network configurations can be software controlled and altered while they continue to be in-use, with transparency to the end users. Most of the network router vendors provide software and network equipment to support SDN capabilities. An SDN can be responsive to information or commands sent from IDS / IPS network monitoring tools, informing the SDN to reconfigure its IP address assignments to avert DDoS sensed attacks. In doing so, the DDoS attacks are 'starved off' and cease, until the hacker is able to find the new network address and location information. Since the attacker IPs will not be provided the new network topology information, it will frustrate and avert the attacks. SDN capabilities are quick, and can change the topology 'on the fly' as often as needed. The SDN can also be used to change in / out equipment used in a network virtual topology. So, not only IP addresses, but also the topology of equipment can be changed with transparency to end users.

Microsoft Server OS Concepts
items.description: Microsoft has this concept for their Server OS versions, using Active Directory (AD) services. Multiple software services can be on a server, known as a TREE. A collection of TREEs that are in one AD domain are known as a FOREST. One of the TREEs will be designated as the primary and inbound / outbound network AD domain point for the other associated TREEs (members) is a collection known as a FOREST (of TREEs, members of the AD domain). The Primary TREE can have one or more designated Secondary TREE(s) that will automatically take over as the Primary... in case the original Primary TREE's "heart beat" indicator becomes silent to the designated Secondary TREE. A whole FOREST can be replicated to have another FOREST take over its operations, if needed.
